title: Characterization of the ribosomal stress response pathway leading to cell cycle arrest in Arabidopsis thaliana
content:
Abstract
When ribosome biogenesis or function is perturbed, plant cells undergo ribosomal stress, leading to growth defects and developmental alterations. The plant ribosomal stress response has recently gained recognition, but its molecular mechanism remains elusive. Here, we characterized this response in Arabidopsis thaliana using ribosome biogenesis-impairing mutations [root initiation defective 2 (rid2) and rid3] and ribosome biogenesis/function-interfering drugs (5-fluorouracil and puromycin) as ribosomal stressors. These stressors repressed cell proliferation and increased ploidy levels indicative of endoreduplication. Under these ribosomal stress conditions, a subset of NAM, ATAF1/2, CUC (NAC) transcription factor genes and cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) inhibitor genes were upregulated, while they tended to downregulate G2/M-specific genes. Overexpression of ANAC082, which encodes an Arabidopsis NAC (ANAC) factor implicated in the ribosomal stress response pathway, phenocopied the ribosomal stress response in terms of cellular behavior and gene expression. These results together indicate that, predominantly mediated by ANAC082, ribosomal stress arrests the cell cycle at G2 and promotes endoreduplication. A comparison of gene expression and genetic relations between the ribosomal and DNA damage stress responses, focusing on ANAC082 and the DNA damage stress response-mediating NAC factor SUPPRESSOR OF GAMMA RESPONSE1, revealed that these stress response pathways are distinct and largely independent of each other, although they have similar outputs in the control of cell proliferation and endoreduplication.
